$comment: DELIBERATELY NON-ACTIVE WORKFLOWS — consumed by scripts/ci/check-workflow-lane-states.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#3345). A disabled workflow produces no runs, so it is
invisible to `gh run list` and to the Actions dashboard: a switched-off lane and a
lane with nothing to do render identically. The state lives in one place only —
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/workflows --paginate \
--jq '.workflows[] | select(.state != "active") | "\(.state)\t\(.path)"'
Disabling happens in the GitHub UI: one click, no commit, no review, no record.
This file IS the record. Anything non-active and absent from here fails the build.
RULES OF THE ALLOWLIST (enforced by the script, not by convention):
1. `path` and `state` must match what the API reports. A state that drifts from
the recorded one FAILS — the old reason does not get to cover a new fact.
2. `owner` is required. #3345 asks for an owner per disablement, not just a note.
3. `reason` must be at least 60 characters and free of TODO/TBD/WIP placeholders.
State what was turned off, what was MEASURED about it, and what has to be true
to turn it back on. Do not state a motive you did not establish
(.claude/rules/deploy-integrity.md R7).
4. `reviewBy` (YYYY-MM-DD) is required and EXPIRES. Past its date the guard fails
until someone re-enables, retires, or re-dates with a fresh read. Without an
expiry a disablement is permanent by default, which is how a lane stays dark
for months while every dashboard reads green.
5. An entry whose lane is ACTIVE again — or gone from the API — FAILS. A register
nobody drains stops describing reality.
RE-ENABLING IS NOT THIS GUARD'S JOB, and must never be made to be. Read the lane's
`schedule:` and its teardown `if:` FIRST. Both sovereign lanes once carried a
cron-reachable teardown (`!inputs.keep_resources` is `!''` = TRUE on a schedule),
so "just turn it back on" would have destroyed a sovereign estate. See
scripts/ci/check-teardown-not-on-schedule.mjs. Enabling is an operator decision.
